questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: A chaconne and its bass pattern
questions.stem: In my marine biologist tank notes of March 4 I observe a movement repeating a short bass pattern throughout.

options.text: That pattern is the ground of a chaconne.
That pattern is the subject of a fugue.
That pattern is the refrain of a rondo.
That pattern is a free episode.

questions.explanation: A repeating short bass pattern throughout a movement is the ground of a chaconne. Subject, refrain, and episode describe other forms.
questions.hint: Repeating bass pattern is the ground.

provenance.author: bank-team-music-theory
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: Counting the statements of a chaconne
questions.stem: My April 6 tank log counts a chaconne whose four-measure ground repeats eight times.
questions.explanation: Eight repetitions of the ground appear in the log. The count of statements equals the repetition count.

provenance.author: bank-team-music-theory
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: Why a rondo's refrain keeps returning
questions.stem: On May 8 my tank notes ask why the rondo refrain keeps coming back between episodes.

answer.exemplar: The refrain returns to provide a familiar anchor between contrasting episodes, giving the movement its recurring structural identity.

questions.explanation: The refrain returns as a familiar anchor between contrasting episodes. Without it the form would lose its recurring identity.

provenance.author: bank-team-music-theory
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: How much of a rondo its refrains take

stimulus.body: Log: a rondo movement of twenty measures has refrains occupying twelve measures total.

questions.stem: My June 10 tank log asks what proportion of the movement the refrains take.
questions.explanation: Twelve of twenty measures is three fifths. Two fifths or one half misstates the proportion.

provenance.author: bank-team-music-theory

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: What a development does to the themes
questions.stem: On September 16 my tank notes ask what the development section does to the themes.

answer.exemplar: The development fragments, modulates, and recombines the themes, creating tension before the recapitulation returns them to the tonic.

questions.explanation: The development transforms and destabilizes the themes. Simply restating them would be a recapitulation, not a development.
